route_steps.visible_checkpoint: Check your Magic level . You need at least 33 for Telekinetic Grab, then unboosted 54 before the Lvl-4 Enchant room: a Wizard's mind bomb supplies the remaining +3 to cast the level-57 spell. Use ordinary elemental combat spells on safe, low-defence targets and buy runes in small batches until you reach the needed level; keep the MTA law/nature/cosmic stock separate. MTA also awards Magic XP as you complete its rooms, so recheck your level before buying more combat runes. If you already have 54, skip the extra training. For the MTA runes, use Lundail's shop inside the Mage Arena bank in deep Wilderness and bring your bank to at least: 1,650 nature runes 700 law runes 500 chaos runes 400 cosmic runes 500 water runes Do not carry the full 1.35m through Wilderness. Bank your valuable kit and coins before the dangerous approach, bring only disposable travel gear, and withdraw purchase money after reaching the safe Mage Arena bank. The bank/shop is safe, but the route to it is not; Hardcore players can instead complete The Feud plus Rogue Trader's rune-shop section and buy from Ali Morrisane in Al Kharid at a higher price. Buy an air staff, earth staff and fire staff from Zaff in Varrock if missing, plus 10 Wizard's mind bombs from Falador's Rising Sun Inn. These supplies are for your MTA visit. Buy small top-ups if you run short before finishing the point targets below.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: The entire reason for MTA here is Bones to Peaches. The spell costs 200 Telekinetic, 300 Alchemist, 2,000 Enchantment and 200 Graveyard pizazz points . Finish the unlock in this visit so MTA does not remain an open chore for the next ten hours. Use these buffered point targets and room loops: Graveyard — 211 points: take bones from a pile, cast Bones to Bananas , deposit the bananas in the chute, and eat bananas when you need healing. Repeat until the point target is reached. Telekinetic — 211 points: position yourself on the side of the maze that pulls the guardian toward the next opening, then cast Telekinetic Grab . Complete each maze rather than abandoning it halfway through. Alchemist — 311 points: the cabinet values rotate. Alch the item currently worth 30 coins ; ignore poor-value items. Low Alchemy works. If a Wizard's Mind Bomb gives you High Alchemy, use it for faster casts. Enchantment — 2,165 points: use the highest enchantment spell you can cast reliably. With the route's level range, Lvl-4 Enchant with a Wizard's Mind Bomb is the intended option. Prioritize the current bonus shape/corner, enchant shapes, then drop them after they score. At the rewards shop, buy 1 mud rune and 10 mist runes , then buy Bones to Peaches . The unlock requires 60 Magic, boostable : check your actual level after the room XP, train to unboosted 57 if needed, then use a Wizard's mind bomb for +3 if needed. When the spell is unlocked, MTA is finished for Chapter 1. Keep any remaining nature runes banked. In 2.1, you will buy more as needed to alch 1,590 battlestaves, using the profits from each batch to fund the next.

preparation.title: The twelve foundation quests: supplies and recovery
preparation.text: Rebank between quests. The quantities below are per quest; a bar, loaf or vial handed in earlier is already spent. Use the material suppliers below for missing basics, and bring food plus a bank teleport for fights. Demon Slayer: 1 coin, a bucket of water and 25 unnoted ordinary bones . Kill chickens/cows and bank the bones until you have 25; ashes and big bones do not substitute. The three keys and Silverlight come from the quest. Keep Silverlight for Shadow of the Storm. A Porcine of Interest: 1 rope, a knife or suitable slash weapon, combat gear and food. Buy rope from Ned in Draynor; a knife avoids relying on whether your weapon can cut the vines. Vampyre Slayer: hammer and 2 coins for Morgan's requested beer at Varrock's Blue Moon Inn. Dr Harlow supplies the stake after the dialogue; carry it and the hammer during the fight. Below Ice Mountain: 1 cooked meat, 1 bread, knife and 3 coins. Buy raw beef and flour from Wydin in Port Sarim, cook the beef and make bread; do not substitute chicken or fish for cooked meat. The quest provides its other sandwich ingredients. The Golem: 4 soft clay, 1 empty vial, pestle and mortar and 1 papyrus. Buy papyrus from Aemad in East Ardougne; mine four clay south-west of Varrock and soften with water. Collect the phoenix feather and black mushrooms during the quest. Shadow of the Storm: Silverlight, 1 separate silver bar, 3 accepted dark clothing items, combat runes and food. Buy priest gown top and bottom from Thessalia in Varrock and a black wizard hat from Betty in Port Sarim; ordinary dark-looking gear is not automatically accepted. Pick a black mushroom in Uzer and use it directly on Silverlight to darken the blade. Use the quest mould and silver bar at a furnace for the demonic sigil; Silverlight must deal the finishing blow. The Lost Tribe: pickaxe, lit candle and tinderbox. Buy a candle from Catherby's candle shop if missing. Use the castle-cellar route and stay on the quest's marked cave path; a candle is not safe for exploring swamp gas elsewhere. Keep the quest's brooch and notes until its dialogue has consumed them. Enter the Abyss: no outside quest ingredient is consumed. The Mage of Zamorak supplies the scrying orb; carry it to the three required essence-mine teleports. Bank valuables before meeting him in low Wilderness, then continue his Varrock-chaos-temple dialogue. Merlin's Crystal: 1 fresh bread, tinderbox, empty bucket and combat gear. Take insect repellent from the Catherby house north of the bank, then use the bucket on the beehives for wax. Kill a bat near Keep Le Faye for bat bones; the quest supplies Excalibur. Keep that sword for Holy Grail. The Dig Site: 2 ropes, 1 empty vial, pestle and mortar, tinderbox and 1 cup of tea from the Varrock tea stall. A cut or uncut opal can be obtained by panning at the Digsite, and charcoal by searching its specimen trays. Collect the exam/panning tools there; no Shilo Village gem access is needed. Elemental Workshop I: knife, pickaxe, hammer, needle, thread, soft leather and 4 coal . Tan one cowhide into soft leather at Ellis in Al Kharid; buy needle/thread at Dommik nearby. Mine coal at 30 Mining, or buy it from Ordan after the first boat trip into Keldagrim (that trip starts The Giant Dwarf; finish it at Step 13). Keep the battered key and elemental shield. Elemental Workshop II: the same pickaxe/hammer/key and 8 new coal . Check that you have 30 Smithing before starting; the earlier four coal are spent. If the key is lost, search the bookcase in the house south of the Seers' Village workshop, then use a knife on the battered book. Make and retain the mind helmet/shield as the quest directs.

preparation.title: Reusable suppliers for this chapter's missing materials
preparation.text: Check the bank first, then buy or make only the shortfall. If you need more coins, return to the Wealthy Citizen method from Chapter 1.2. Restock items used in earlier quests before packing for the next one. Tools and containers: general stores such as Lumbridge's sell hammer, chisel, tinderbox, buckets and pots. Take a knife from the Lumbridge Castle kitchen/cellar spawn or buy one from Ardougne's spice seller. Dommik in Al Kharid sells needle, thread, jewellery/sickle/holy moulds; the Varrock Sawmill sells saws and nails. Ned in Draynor sells rope; buy balls of wool from Aemad's Adventuring Supplies in East Ardougne, or shear sheep north of Lumbridge and spin their wool at the castle's first-floor spinning wheel (1 Crafting). Sarah's farm shop south of Falador sells farming tools, plant pots, compost and cure. Buy an empty item when the quest asks for empty; fill water containers at a sink or fountain. Bars and wire: use a furnace to smelt one copper + one tin into bronze (1 Smithing), iron ore into iron (15, with failed smelts possible), or one iron + two coal into steel (30). Smith one bronze bar into one bronze wire at 4 Smithing. Mine the basic ore south-east/south-west of Varrock; coal requires 30 Mining, or buy it from Ordan after the boat into Keldagrim. Gold needs 40 Smithing. The first Keldagrim boat trip starts The Giant Dwarf automatically; shopping there does not complete the quest. Planks / leather / clay / glass: cut the required tree and pay the Varrock Sawmill to convert its logs into the required plank type. Kill a cow and pay Ellis in Al Kharid for soft or hard leather as specified. Mine clay south-west of Varrock and add water for soft clay. Charter traders sell buckets of sand and soda ash; smelt one of each at a furnace for one molten glass. Take a glassblowing pipe from the house west of Entrana's furnace (bank weapons/armour before the boat) and use it on the glass for the required item. Make any extra quest glass from additional sand and soda ash, keeping the planned 1,600-glass batch below for its listed uses. Food ingredients: Wydin in Port Sarim sells flour, redberries and raw beef/chicken. Water + flour makes bread dough; bake it on a range. For a redberry pie, make pastry dough, put it in a pie dish, add redberries and bake at 10 Cooking; a pie dish spawns in Varrock Palace's kitchen. Milk a dairy cow with an empty bucket and collect eggs at Lumbridge farms. Repeat if food burns. Ordinary cooked fish for travel can come from the Fishing bank or a short Catherby catch-and-cook refill. Low-level herbs: check the bank for the requested herb first. If the requested marrentill, tarromin, harralander or ranarr is missing, take combat gear, food and a bank teleport to the chaos druids near the entrance of Taverley Dungeon. Bank the matching herb drops until you have enough; the drops are random, so this may take several trips. Sanfew in Taverley sells water-filled vials and pestle and mortar. Clean the herb at its Herblore level, or pay Zahur in Nardah 200 coins per herb if the requested clean herb is above your level. A herb added to water is an unfinished potion, not a finished combat potion. Enclosed light when a cave needs it: at 26 Smithing, smith one extra iron bar into an oil-lantern frame. Blow one freshly sourced molten glass into an oil lamp at 12 Crafting, then combine frame and lamp at 26 Crafting. Pick up one swamp tar in Lumbridge Swamp, use it on the Chemist's lamp-oil still west of Rimmington, fill the lantern and light it with a tinderbox at 26 Firemaking. This gives an oil lantern , not an exposed oil lamp; carry the tinderbox in case it goes out. If you need more Crafting or Smithing levels, train with spare glass or bars before a quest takes you into a cave that needs this lantern. Candles are adequate only where the quest note specifically uses them. Quest-supplied keys, moulds, letters and special plants stay with the quest until its steps consume them. Use the shops and methods above for ordinary ingredients. If a special quest item is missing, use Quest Helper to find the NPC or container that replaces it.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: Complete these as standalone quests, in this order: Demon Slayer A Porcine of Interest — the 1,000 Slayer XP combines with the Varrock Museum Natural History Quiz to comfortably clear Desert Treasure's 10 Slayer requirement. Vampyre Slayer Below Ice Mountain The Golem Shadow of the Storm — put the selectable 10,000 combat XP into Ranged The Lost Tribe Enter the Abyss miniquest — finish it completely so Abyss access is unlocked Merlin's Crystal The Dig Site Elemental Workshop I Elemental Workshop II — if you are still below 30 Smithing, use Giant Foundry or ordinary bars to reach 30 first Before Shadow of the Storm: check that one of the quest-reserved silver bars from 1.1 remains for its crafted demonic sigil. If it was spent, buy one replacement from the East Ardougne Silver Merchant before this quest; do not count optional jewellery as a replacement. Finish each quest before moving to the next. The Dig Site is especially important because it feeds both Fossil Island and Desert Treasure; Enter the Abyss unlocks a useful route to Runecraft altars. By this point you are comfortably over 32 Quest Points . Go upstairs in the Champions' Guild and buy from Scavvo : 1 rune sword — specifically the rune sword , not the rune longsword 1 green d'hide chaps 1 green d'hide vambraces Keep all three. The rune sword is the simple melee weapon used through the rest of Chapter 1 and early Chapter 2, and the green d'hide is useful early Ranged/quest gear. Before leaving the bank: check the quest-specific quantities and sources in the preparation note.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: Gather the sand for your glassmaking batch. Withdraw a pickaxe, desert clothing, waterskins/food, about 80,000 gp , and the 1,600 noted empty buckets banked in 1.2. Go to the Desert Quarry / Sandstorm grinder and give the noted buckets to Drew . Mine sandstone and deposit every piece into Sandstorm . Continue until the grinder is holding enough processed sand for 1,600 buckets . Sand yield depends on sandstone size, so the target is the grinder total—not 1,600 individual rocks. Pay Drew 50 gp per bucket and withdraw exactly 1,600 buckets of sand . That costs 80,000 gp . Mining-level choice: staying at sandstone until roughly 43 Mining is a quick way to gain more Mining XP. If the 1,600 buckets of sand is already finished and you are tired of the desert, leave immediately and finish the level at Shooting Stars instead. After the sand is banked, use tier 4 or lower Shooting Stars with your best available pickaxe for the relaxed route; use a rune pickaxe if you already have one. Continue until you have both 44 Mining and 2,000 total stardust . If 44 Mining comes first, keep mining stars until 2,000 stardust. Do not spend the stardust: early Chapter 2 buys the Celestial ring with all 2,000.

route_steps.review: Eight clay bracelets are optional; the full materials bill includes them and skipping all eight saves eight gold bars, eight sapphires and eight cosmics. Enchant only chosen unfinished items from the live cosmic balance; MTA stock is shared. Both tablet consumers accept ordinary clay plus water.

preparation.title: Moulds, wool and enchantment runes
preparation.text: Buy ring, necklace, amulet and bracelet moulds from Dommik in Al Kharid . Use cut gems and gold bars at a furnace; amulets additionally need one ball of wool each before enchanting. Aemad's Adventuring Supplies in East Ardougne sells balls of wool, or shear sheep north of Lumbridge and spin their wool at Lumbridge Castle's first-floor wheel (1 Crafting). Necklaces and rings do not require wool. Enchant only the pieces being made, using one cosmic rune per enchantment on the standard spellbook : Lvl-1 Enchant uses 1 cosmic + 1 water per sapphire item, Lvl-2 uses 1 cosmic + 3 air per emerald item, and Lvl-3 uses 1 cosmic + 5 fire per ruby item. Equip the matching elemental staff to cover those elemental runes. Buy cosmic shortfalls from Ali Morrisane's unlocked rune shop or Lundail using the travel precautions in Step 1; check what is left after MTA before buying more. Bracelets of clay use sapphire bracelets and Lvl-1 Enchant; the binding necklace uses an emerald necklace. All eight optional bracelets use eight cosmic runes and eight sapphires; those sapphires are already included in the 20-sapphire total. If short on cosmics when you reach the clay step, use its ordinary-clay-and-water option instead of restocking and switching spellbooks just for bracelets.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: Unlock digsite pendants before enchanting ruby necklaces. After The Dig Site, clean uncleaned finds in the Varrock Museum until you uncover a clean necklace (random; keep cleaning until it appears). Show it to an archaeologist in the cleaning area to learn the special Lvl-3 Enchant recipe. Then make/enchant the ruby necklaces at 49 Magic , which you reached before MTA. Ordinary ruby-necklace enchantment does not automatically work before this unlock; count any Kudos earned here toward Step 6. Once your Crafting level allows it, make at least the following working stack: 20 rings of dueling 10 digsite pendants 10 games necklaces 5 necklaces of passage if jade and silver are already banked ; otherwise defer this convenience stock The full Chapter 1 target is 40 rings of dueling, 45 digsite pendants and 10 games necklaces , plus 2 sapphire amulets, 1 ruby amulet and 1 binding necklace and up to 8 optional bracelets of clay . The bracelets save the water-softening step when mining clay; skip them if you prefer to mine ordinary clay and use water for the tablets in 1.4 and 2.1. From an empty jewelry bank, including all eight bracelets, this is 107 gold bars, 41 emeralds, 46 rubies and 20 sapphires ; skipping all eight reduces that to 99 gold bars and 12 sapphires , with the same emerald/ruby totals; the five separate jade passage necklaces take five additional silver bars if chosen. Never spend the remaining quest-reserved silver bars on those optional necklaces. Count finished pieces and gems before sourcing anything. Wintertodt/Tempoross rewards are variable, not a guarantee. For missing precious gems before Shilo Village, keep the 2,000 stardust reserved for the Celestial ring untouched and mine extra Shooting Stars for the low-attention route: each additional 300 stardust buys a 40-gem bag from Dusuri at the Mining Guild entrance. Contents vary, so open bags as you go and stop when you have the missing gems. Alternatively, the East Ardougne gem merchant sells stocked cut sapphire, emerald and ruby gems, but its low per-world stock makes a large refill repetitive. For missing gold bars, buy only the required gold ore from Ordan at Blast Furnace in Keldagrim or mine it; if below 40 Smithing, train to 40 with ordinary iron/steel work, then smelt gold at a furnace or Blast Furnace. Jade is not supplied by those star bags: if absent, leave passage necklaces for Shilo Village gem rocks after the quest in 2.2 and use ordinary travel in the meantime. Before leaving the bank: check the quest-specific quantities and sources in the preparation note.

preparation.title: Priest in Peril, Bone Voyage and the first camp bank
preparation.text: Priest in Peril: empty bucket, combat supplies and 50 unnoted rune or pure essence . Mine any deficit using Aubury's Varrock essence teleport after Rune Mysteries; deliver it in multiple trips. Keep the bucket for the blessed-water sequence. Bone Voyage: 2 vodka + 1 marrentill potion (unf) . Buy vodka from Heckel Funch in the Grand Tree. Put one clean marrentill in a vial of water at 5 Herblore; do not add unicorn horn dust. If no herb remains, use the herb recovery below. The Apothecary makes the potion of sealegs from these ingredients after the quest dialogue. Fossil Island camp: prioritise the bank chest with 2 oak planks, 1 iron bar, 5 nails, hammer and saw at 21 Construction. Buy saw/nails and convert two cut oak logs at the Varrock Sawmill if missing. If below 21, do the Construction catch-up immediately below first. Other camp facilities are optional conveniences; they are not a condition for birdhouse runs. Wear leather gloves and leather boots and collect the trowel, rock pick and specimen brush from the museum's tool rack for cleaning finds. Buy replacement leather gloves and boots from a general or clothing shop; combat vambraces do not work here. Bring a pickaxe for the volcanic-ash stop; the 1,000-ash target is separate from the quest inventory.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: Complete Priest in Peril first. Then go to the Varrock Museum and reach the 100 Kudos needed for Bone Voyage: Complete the Natural History Quiz in the museum basement if you have not already. Take the Hunter and Slayer XP. Talk to Historian Minas and tell him about every completed quest he will accept for Kudos. Check your total. If you are below 100 Kudos , use the museum cleaning area and complete unidentified-cleaned-find displays until the total reaches at least 100. Once the museum shows 100+ Kudos , complete Bone Voyage . On Fossil Island, build the camp facilities you can build and unlock the Mushroom Meadow, Verdant Valley and House on the Hill mushtrees . Use a digsite pendant on the strange machine in the House on the Hill so future pendants can teleport there directly. While you are already on the island, mine and bank at least 1,000 volcanic ash ; this becomes ultracompost later. Before leaving the bank: check the quest-specific quantities and sources in the preparation note.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: Make the first four clockworks: at 25+ Construction , add a POH workshop if needed, build crafting table 1 with four oak planks , then upgrade it to crafting table 2 with one molten glass set aside for this table. A new workshop costs 10,000 coins ; buy the four oak planks by converting oak logs at the sawmill if needed. Use four steel bars on the table (one per clockwork). Check for banked bars first; smelt any shortfall from iron ore and coal. The clockworks return when you harvest completed bird houses, so these are not four new bars every run. Bring each run: a hammer, chisel, 4 clockworks , 4 logs for the highest birdhouse tier you can currently make , 40 cheap bait seeds , and a digsite pendant. Low-level hop seeds such as barley or hammerstone from Olivia's Draynor Seed Market remain an easy default; eligible flower and allotment seeds also work. Keep the seeds you plan to plant or use in quests banked; use spare bait seeds for birdhouses. Ten low-level seeds fill each house, so 40 seeds cover one complete run. Restock as needed. Use each clockwork on a log to make 4 bird houses . Teleport to the House on the Hill . Mushtree to Verdant Valley and place the two bird houses there. Mushtree to Mushroom Meadow , place the bird house there, then run south to the Tar Swamp entrance and place the fourth. Use 10 cheap seeds on each bird house . After roughly 50 minutes , harvest all four. You get the clockworks back; bring four replacement logs and another 40 seeds next run. Fit runs around your session: do birdhouses when you log in, finish a quest, or want a two-minute break. The Hunter XP adds up over time; there is no need to set an alarm. Chapter 2 teak preparation: save the first 2 teak seeds you receive from bird nests/contracts. Do not spend them elsewhere. You cannot plant them until 35 Farming ; 1.4 explains when to turn them into saplings and start the roughly three-day growth timer.

preparation.title: RFD opening, Goblins, Mountain Dwarf and Pirate Pete
preparation.text: Opening cook: 1 eye of newt from Betty in Port Sarim, 1 Greenman's ale from Yanille's Dragon Inn, 1 rotten tomato from the crate by Varrock's pillory, ashes from a burnt log, and a fruit blast you make yourself . Buy a cocktail shaker, cocktail glass, 1 pineapple, 2 lemons and 1 orange from the Grand Tree's cocktail/grocery shops; mix a fruit blast in the shaker, pour it, and garnish with a slice cut from the second lemon using a knife. Then add the ashes for the dirty blast. A premade fruit blast does not work. Goblin generals: fresh bread, orange, knife, blue/green/purple dye, spice or gnome spice, fishing bait, bucket of water and charcoal. Buy orange/spice from the Grand Tree or unlocked Culinaromancer's Chest, bait from Gerrant, charcoal from Jiminua. For a new blue dye, pay Wyson in Falador Park 20 coins for 2 woad leaves, then give both leaves and 5 coins to Aggie in Draynor. Prepare the unusual coloured/soggy food during the subquest. Mountain Dwarf: 320 coins, bucket of milk, pot of flour, egg, bowl of water and 4 Asgarnian ales (buy the ales from Kaylee in Falador's Rising Sun Inn). The unlocked chest sells milk/flour/egg; the Lumbridge basement has a bowl and sink. Wear ordinary leather gloves to pick up the hot rock cake, then kill an Ice Mountain icefiend to cool it. Ice gloves are a convenience here, not a new mandatory detour. Keep the dwarven rock cake afterwards. Pirate Pete: empty fishbowl, needle, pestle and mortar, knife, 3 bronze wire , raw cod and fresh bread. Smith three bronze bars into three wire at 4 Smithing (each bar is one copper + one tin); these are separate from Fenkenstrain's later three wires. Buy a big fishing net from Harry in Catherby and fish there for a raw cod at 23 Fishing if none remains. Murphy supplies the diving gear during the quest; keep it. Catch the underwater ingredients there, and replace cod/bread if the fishcake burns.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: If Cook's Assistant is not complete, finish it first. If none is banked, blow one from one of the two spare molten glass at your 46+ Crafting (the fishbowl needs 42). Blowing it gives 42.5 Crafting XP. Keep the other spare molten glass for Chapter 2, along with the glass set aside for Desert Treasure and The Hand in the Sand. Your 1.2 quest work and 60 Cooking make this a clean time to close all three rather than starting them and carrying their ingredients through half the chapter. Combined with the 1,000 XP from A Porcine of Interest and 1,000 XP from the Varrock Museum Natural History Quiz, you will have at least 3,000 Slayer XP (level 16) . Part 1.4 will use one short Slayer assignment to close the remaining 523 XP to level 18 before Animal Magnetism. preparation.title: Raw fish for the lyre and Mountain Daughter's crossing
preparation.text: The Fremennik Trials: bring 5,250 coins, tinderbox, knife, axe and 1 raw shark, raw manta ray or raw sea turtle . Wait for stock or try another world if bought out. Do not cook this offering and do not grind 76 Fishing for it. Check that you have 25 Fletching/40 Woodcutting if making the lyre; these are below this route's established targets. Koschei's final form need not be defeated. Mountain Daughter: 1 rope, pickaxe, axe, any plank, leather gloves and an elemental staff or the pole from the goat pen north of Hamal's tent. Buy a normal plank from the sawmill by converting one ordinary log if none remains; keep food and your combat weapon for the Kendal.

preparation.title: Sickle, serum and conductor ingredients
preparation.text: Nature Spirit: ghostspeak amulet and silver sickle. Use one silver bar with a sickle mould bought from Dommik at a furnace (18 Crafting). Join the official Shades of Mort'ton world for temple repair, buy timber/limestone/swamp paste and olive oil in Mort'ton, sanctify the oil at the charged temple and use it on the log. preparation.title: Lost City equipment and your three Fairytale I items
preparation.text: Lost City: reach 31 Crafting/36 Woodcutting, bring a knife, combat runes and food, and bank weapons/armour before boarding for Entrana. Kill the dungeon zombies for a bronze axe, use Magic from behind the mushrooms against the tree spirit, then cut dramen branches and knife them into staffs. Make one working staff and at least one spare for recovery; you cannot take a normal axe through the monks' equipment check. Fairytale I: dramen staff, ghostspeak amulet, spade and secateurs from Sarah's farm shop south of Falador. Dig the Draynor skull from the grave north of the manor when asked. Read Malignius's three-item request before shopping; use the branch table below. Bring a filled druid pouch for edible items crossing Mort Myre: Bloom with the blessed sickle, collect extra swamp produce and fill the pouch without consuming a requested pear/stem/fungus. Collect only the three items you were asked for. These methods work with your current skills and offer alternatives to growing high-level crops or herbs: White berries: kill chaos druid warriors in Yanille Agility Dungeon (40 Agility) for one; stay away from the chaos altar that drops you into poison spiders. Mort myre pear / stem / fungus: Bloom with the blessed sickle beside a bush / branch / rotten log respectively; collect the required produce loose. Nature talisman: if no reward/drop is banked, buy one for 50 abyssal pearls from Apprentice Felix at Guardians of the Rift after Temple of the Eye. If Temple of the Eye is unfinished, first reach 10 Runecraft (Enter the Abyss is already done; mine rune essence through Aubury and craft air runes at the altar south of Falador for the small remaining XP gap; if the air talisman is missing, kill the air wizard beside Malignius Mortifer north-west of Port Sarim until it drops one), then take a bucket of water, pickaxe and chisel to Wizard Persten north of Al Kharid and complete its tutorial. For normal rounds, enter the basement rift below the Wizards' Tower with pickaxe/chisel: mine guardian fragments, make guardian essence, craft at the active altars you can use, then deliver the resulting stones to the Great Guardian. Earn both elemental and catalytic energy, claim rewards and stop once you have 50 pearls. Only take this detour if you need the talisman. Fairy rings are not available until after this quest. Clean avantoe / irit leaf: get the grimy herb from banked drops or Taverley chaos druids; if below 48 / 40 Herblore, pay Zahur in Nardah 200 coins to clean the requested herb. Do not turn it into an unfinished potion. Blue dragon scale: take an anti-dragon shield and pick a ground scale in Taverley Dungeon's blue-dragon chamber. If you do not have the shield yet, start Dragon Slayer I at the Champions' Guild and obtain it from Duke Horacio first. Below 70 Agility, free Velrak in the Black Knights' base for the dusty key. Bring antipoison, food and a teleport; no dragon kill is required. Proboscis / volencia moss: do Jungle Potion now if either is rolled, then collect mosquito proboscis during Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup or clean the moss from the jungle-mine rocks. Skip Jungle Potion when it appears again later, and still check your Herblore level before Eadgar's Ruse. Jangerberries / lime: use banked Hosidius fruit-stall produce; otherwise steal jangerberries there at 25 Thieving and buy a lime from the Grand Tree. Potato cactus: take a rope, antipoison, food and a teleport to the Kalphite Lair west of Shantay Pass. Use the entrance rope and collect a ground potato cactus near the soldiers; no seed or 64 Farming is required. Crushed gem / unopened oyster: pan at the Digsite for opals/oysters. Keep an oyster unopened. Cut spare opals with a chisel until one fails into a crushed gem; a cut opal is not a substitute. Clean snapdragon: the Brimhaven Agility Arena sells one for 10 Brimhaven vouchers. At this route's 50+ Agility, tag consecutive active ticket dispensers until you have 10 Brimhaven vouchers, and buy one herb from Pirate Jackie the Fruit. Keep the herb clean and unmixed for the quest. Supercompost: put 15 pineapples from a charter shop in an empty compost bin, close it, then return after rotting and take one bucket of supercompost. This is separate from Garden of Tranquillity's later reward. Babydragon bones: kill a baby blue dragon in Taverley Dungeon; use the same dusty-key route as the scale. Jogre bones: kill a jogre in Pothole Dungeon on Karamja. These are specific bones, not ordinary or adult dragon bones. Uncut diamond / uncut ruby: use banked uncut gems or the extra-stardust gem bags from Step 5, preserving the 2,000 ring reserve. Stop when the requested uncut stone appears; a cut gem will not work. Raw cave eel / raw slimy eel: fishing rod and bait from Gerrant, plus a lit enclosed oil lantern, for Lumbridge Swamp Caves; 38 / 28 Fishing respectively. Enter through the Lost Tribe castle route and avoid cave hazards. Keep the fish raw. The lantern recipe is in the material-suppliers note. Edible seaweed: pick the edible-seaweed spawn on Fossil Island's north-east coast; ordinary seaweed is different. Red vine worm: dig in McGrubor's Wood with a spade. Fat snail: kill a bruise or blood blamish snail in Mort Myre and keep its raw meat. Charcoal: Jiminua's Jungle Store. Red spiders' eggs: ground spawns by the moss giants at the west end of Varrock Sewers, with a knife for webs. Grapes: the now-unlocked Culinaromancer's Chest. King worm: ground spawns north-west in the Gnome Stronghold. Snape grass: ground spawns west of the Crafting Guild. For Tanglefoot, equip the magic secateurs ; ordinary weapons cannot finish this fight. Without 43 Prayer yet, use the mushroom/corridor flinch: hit once, return behind the obstacle and wait for its health bar to disappear before the next hit. Bring food for mistakes and bank the spare dramen staff in Zanaris.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: Complete Lost City , then complete Fairytale I – Growing Pains . Bring the ghostspeak amulet banked in 1.1 when Quest Helper asks for it. Check your bank for those items, then collect whichever are missing. Do not leave the quest at the request stage—complete it to collect the Farming XP below. Why Fairytale I is here: it awards 3,500 Farming XP . That is enough to clear the 17 Farming requirement for Forgettable Tale even if you started with essentially no Farming XP. preparation.title: Keldagrim errands and the complete kelda brewing kit
preparation.text: The Giant Dwarf: bring at least 2,500 coins plus a purchase buffer, a log, tinderbox, 1 coal, 1 iron bar, 3 cut sapphires, 1 law + 1 air rune for Telekinetic Grab, and a fresh redberry pie for Thurgo unless you already gave him an extra. Ordan sells coal/ore, the city jeweller sells cut sapphires, and a furnace turns iron ore into an iron bar at 15 Smithing. Bake the pie from flour/water/pie dish/redberries at 10 Cooking. Company errands request variable ores and bars: accept the task, buy its ore from Ordan and smelt any requested bars at the relevant Smithing level, then return before the timer expires. Let an awkward high-tier request expire and ask again; keep the silver for Animal Magnetism and Desert Treasure banked, and buy other ores only when requested. Forgettable Tale: 500 coins, 2 barley malt, 2 buckets of water, rake, seed dibber, 1 kebab, 3 beers, 1 dwarven stout and an empty beer glass, plus the item requested by the Rowdy dwarf. The Keldagrim food shop sells the kebab and its pubs sell beer; pick up the dwarven stout from the table beside Khorvak in the pub under White Wolf Mountain; drinking a spare beer supplies the glass. If the two barley malt are missing, buy four barley seeds from Olivia in Draynor, plant them in the hops patch north of Lumbridge's cow field with a rake/seed dibber, and use compost/water. At 3+ Farming, harvest the mature barley and cook two on a range to make malt; plain barley does not work. You only need to grow enough barley for the two malt. The quest gives all four kelda seeds; grow them in its special patch, harvest the kelda hops, then add the two waters, two barley malt, hops and yeast to the brewing vat (take the nearby empty pot and pay Blandebir 25 coins for the yeast). Keep the empty glass to draw the finished beer. Wait until the vat is ready, then draw the finished stout and continue the quest.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: Complete The Giant Dwarf . If its variable company errand asks for silver bars, buy those in addition to the remaining quest-reserved bars at the East Ardougne Silver Merchant rather than spending the Animal Magnetism/Desert Treasure stock. Then start Forgettable Tale... and begin the kelda brewing/fermentation step. The Rowdy dwarf's kelda-seed item request varies: ask what he wants, check the bank, and if that particular item is awkward tell him you do not know where to get it to request another item. Gather the requested item once you know what it is. The brew takes time to ferment, so use the wait for another activity. Use the wait for a birdhouse run, a Crafting/Fletching session, or another finished activity. Return when the brew is ready and finish Forgettable Tale completely . These quest rewards prepare you for Farming: The Goblin generals subquest gave 1,000 Farming XP , Fairytale I gives 3,500 , and Forgettable Tale gives 5,000 . That is 9,500 Farming XP before the Zeah block, already enough for 26 Farming . The Garden of Death later in this subsection adds another 10,000 Farming XP , so 1.4 begins with at least 19,500 XP (level 33) . That meets Garden of Tranquillity's Farming requirement for the next section. Before leaving the bank: check the quest-specific quantities and sources in the preparation note.

preparation.text: Death Plateau: 60 coins, 1 premade Blurberry special, 1 iron bar, 10 unnoted bread and 10 unnoted cooked trout . preparation.title: Supplies for every quest in the Zeah block
preparation.text: The Queen of Thieves: 1 stew. Buy a cooked stew from the Seers' Village pub or Warriors' Guild food shop if accessible; the Seers' pub needs no guild entry. Keep it for the quest instead of eating it. The Depths of Despair: no outside quest item; bring combat gear, food and a teleport for the Sand Snake. Its scrolls/key are quest-local. The Forsaken Tower: no outside ingredient; collect the building's tools and puzzle materials during the quest. No pre-banked potion recipe is needed. Tale of the Righteous: pickaxe, rope, a ranged weapon with matching ammunition and runes for a combat spell. Bring both ranged and Magic even if you normally melee. If no ranged weapon/ammunition remain, buy a shortbow and 20 bronze arrows from Lowe in Varrock; take air/mind runes from Aubury or Betty for Wind Strike. Buy more ammunition or runes if you are running short. The Garden of Death: secateurs, obtainable inside the quest or reused from Sarah's shop. Bring food for the surrounding creatures; the tablets and notes are collected along the route. The Ascent of Arceuus: no outside quest ingredient; take combat gear, food and a teleport for the trapped souls. Getting Ahead: 26 Construction, bear fur, 1 soft clay, hammer, saw, 2 normal planks, at least 6 nails (take spares), knife, red dye, flour, needle and thread. The farm supplies the construction/crafting materials when searched; kill a bear west of it for fur. Use those local supplies before buying duplicates, and take any free replacement nails if some bend. Finish and retain the Kharedst's memoirs pages as each quest awards them. If a later teleport is depleted, recharge the book at the Old Memorial using the required runes; check its remaining charges before relying on a teleport.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: How Sulliusceps work: Sulliusceps are giant mushrooms inside the Tar Swamp on Fossil Island . Only one of six locations is active for your character at a time; after you chop the active mushroom down, the next one becomes active and you continue around the route. The first trip is the confusing one. Once the southern teleport is unlocked and you have seen the loop once, repeated clears are much simpler. Bring: your rune axe (or dragon axe if Wintertodt gave you one), a rake , antipoison , plenty of food , Fossil Island access such as a digsite pendant , and a teleport out. Keep several free inventory spaces for caps, fossils and other drops. The swamp has dangerous tar monsters and poisonous spine mushrooms; chopping is fairly low-attention, but moving between spots is not walk-away AFK. Get into the swamp: use the Fossil Island mushtree network to reach Mushroom Meadow , then head south into the Tar Swamp. Cut blocking vines/roots with your axe and rake the ground vines when the route requires it. Unlock Sticky Swamp immediately: on the first lap, activate the Sticky Swamp Magic Mushtree near the southern/bottom part of the route. From then on you can teleport straight back to the useful end of the swamp without walking through the entrance each trip. Avoid the hazards instead of fighting them: do not intentionally fight tar monsters. Keep moving, eat when needed, and use terrain to get away. Antipoison is for the spine-mushroom poison. Follow the rotation: find the active Sulliuscep, chop it until it depletes, then move to the next active location. After your first complete lap, this becomes a repeatable circuit rather than a scavenger hunt. Bank caps if they arrive while training to 70. Five caps can make four mushroom pies later, but they are not a condition for finishing this step. Birdhouse runs do not award Sulliuscep caps. Stop at 70 Woodcutting. Finding five caps may take roughly 45–75 minutes once you know the route, and sometimes longer because the drops are random. Keep any caps you received and continue questing. The coming Crafting rewards may leave you needing little or no extra training, so you do not need to stay here hunting caps. Open the OSRS Wiki Sulliuscep strategy before the first run and keep its swamp-route image handy. Keep useful unidentified fossils you receive; they can be identified for Varrock Museum displays/Kudos later.

preparation.title: Give yourself the best chance to hop before a PKer lands the first hit
preparation.text: Before the first trip, set Private chat to Friends or Off. With Private set to Friends, players who are not on your Friends List see you as offline. That prevents a random PKer from simply adding your name and using private-chat status to follow your world between trips. Keep the logout/world-switch interface ready while you offer bones. A very practical setup is to open the World Switcher and leave the cursor over a different world. If another player logs in beside the altar and has not hit you yet, switch immediately instead of waiting to decide whether they look dangerous. Once you are in combat, you cannot world-hop and must be out of combat for 10 seconds first. Do not always hop to the next world in the list. Choosing a world several entries away makes your destination less predictable because PKers often cycle through worlds looking for altar users. You still need to watch for players after switching worlds. The first hit is the important one. There is very little you can do once a geared PKer has landed a freeze/Tele Block and put you in combat. Your best defence on this low-risk route is noticing the login quickly, hopping before the first attack, and never risking more than one inventory of bones. After using every bone, the Wine of Zamorak offers a quick return to your respawn point. When no player has damaged you, repeatedly taking the wine is a convenient way to die and return to your respawn point instead of running south. Do not rely on the wine to deny a PKer your remaining bones. If another player has already damaged you recently, the death uses Wilderness PvP death rules even if the wine deals the final point of damage; lost tradeable items are awarded under the PvP rules, generally to the player who dealt the most damage. If a PKer appears before touching you, hopping is the better escape attempt.

preparation.title: If you die and your bones are sitting in a dangerous gravestone
preparation.text: You usually do not need to keep death-running a dangerous PvM grave. A normal gravestone lasts for 15 minutes of logged-in time, and you can ask Death to collect its contents for you. Ferox Enclave has access to Death's Office , so if retrieving the grave itself is becoming a second death trap, bank anything you kept and go there instead. The confusing “some items have been moved to Death's Office” message: if you die again while an existing grave already contains lots of normal unstackable items, the grave has a capacity rule. Excess items from the existing grave can be moved to Death's Office before the new death is added. That can make it look as though only the three items you kept on death survived, even though the rest may simply have been transferred to Death. For this route, ordinary dragon bones are individually worth less than 100,000 coins, so reclaiming those low-value items from Death is normally free . Valuable equipment can have reclamation fees, which is another reason the altar trips should contain essentially nothing except disposable bones. Important: this explanation is for an ordinary gravestone/PvM death. A death involving another player in the Wilderness can use different item-loss rules. Always check the Items Kept on Death screen before risking anything you care about.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: Dragonfire-protection check: before equipping the anti-dragon shield for this block, start Dragon Slayer I with the Guildmaster in the Champions' Guild (32 Quest Points are already secured), ask about protection, and collect the shield from Duke Horacio upstairs in Lumbridge Castle. Current mechanics require the quest to be started to equip the shield. The shield protects you while gathering dragon bones; finish the whole quest in 2.2. The dragon bones are the Prayer method, but you do not need to spend the entire grind standing in the Wilderness. Green dragons are much faster and easier to kill, so start there while the area is quiet. If PK traffic becomes annoying—or if you simply do not want to risk another trip—finish the bone stack safely on Isle of Souls blue dragons . The bones are identical for Prayer purposes, so the two methods mix perfectly. Target: aim for roughly 75–80 dragon bones total before using the Chaos Altar. The exact number varies because earlier Prayer XP differs and the altar's 50% bone-save effect is random. If you already trained some extra Prayer, you may need fewer; stop immediately once you reach 43 Prayer . Part A — fast first batch: green dragons near Corporeal Beast Bring: a games necklace , water staff , air runes , chaos runes , mind runes , anti-dragon shield , amulet of magic , a looting bag , and cheap food such as the banked salmon. Wear only gear you are comfortable losing and leave your cash stack in the bank. Use the games necklace to teleport to Corporeal Beast . Leave the cave into the Wilderness and run west to the nearby green dragons. Green dragons have a 50% weakness to Water spells , which is why Water Bolt works so well here. Use Water Bolt while you have spare chaos runes. Preserve your final 100 chaos runes for later Chapter 2 needs; once you approach that reserve, switch to Water Strike . Pick up every dragon bone and every green dragonhide . Put hides in the looting bag first and keep bones in the inventory. Bank early rather than carrying a stack you would hate to lose. Do not force the entire 75–80-bone grind here. Roughly 30–40 green-dragon bones is a good fast first batch, but the real rule is simple: stay while it feels quiet and efficient; leave as soon as PK activity turns the method into a nuisance. Part B — safe finish: Isle of Souls blue dragons If Isle of Souls is new to you: this is a normal non-Wilderness island containing Soul Wars and a small dungeon. You do not need to play Soul Wars or complete its tutorial just to use the island. The easiest route is the Soul Wars minigame teleport , which lands you at Nomad's camp on the Isle of Souls. There is a bank in the Soul Wars lobby, making it a convenient place to resupply between dragon trips. Open the OSRS Wiki Isle of Souls Dungeon page if you want the map beside you on the first run. Getting there: open the Grouping / Minigames interface and use the Soul Wars minigame teleport. If that is unavailable or on cooldown, fairy ring BJP lands on the northern coast of the Isle of Souls; the Soul Wars portal in Edgeville is another fallback. You do not need to enter a Soul Wars match. From the Soul Wars lobby, run north-east across the island to the dungeon entrance on the eastern side of the Isle of Souls and climb down. Dungeon route: follow the dungeon around past the demon room and the fire-giant room. The third main room contains four adult blue dragons and three baby blue dragons . Safespot: the easiest landmark is the small cove containing two adamantite rocks on the eastern side of the blue-dragon room. Walk inside the stalagmites and cast from there; the adult dragons cannot reach you. Keep the anti-dragon shield equipped while moving through the dungeon. Magic: blue dragons also have a 50% Water weakness . Water Bolt is faster if you have spare chaos runes, but Water Strike is completely acceptable here and lets you preserve the 100-chaos-rune Chapter 2 reserve. With the safespot established, this is much lower-stress than the Wilderness method. Bank every dragon bone and, if you have inventory space, the blue dragonhides as well. A looting bag does not help outside the Wilderness, so simply bank at the Soul Wars lobby and run back. Continue until your combined green + blue dragon bones reach roughly 75–80 total . Keep one spare dragon bone banked after reaching 43 Prayer. Watchtower will use it later in this section. Part C — cash the bones in at the correct Wilderness Chaos Altar There are two different Wilderness locations called the Chaos Temple. You want the small Chaos Temple (hut) in level 38 Wilderness, northwest of the Forgotten Cemetery and west of the Lava Maze. Do not use the level ~11 Chaos Temple near Ferox that is packed with Zombie Pirates and aggressive level-129 Elder Chaos Druids. Those druids can hit hard, repeatedly Tele Block you and pull you back toward them. If you see a crowd of druids/pirates, you are at the wrong temple. Open the OSRS Wiki Wilderness map and look for the level-38 Chaos Temple (hut) . Default route: bank all combat gear at Ferox Enclave , take only one disposable inventory of dragon bones , then run north into deep Wilderness toward the Forgotten Cemetery . Continue northwest to the small level-38 temple just south of the Frozen Waste Plateau. If you already have a burning amulet , its Lava Maze teleport is a faster optional route; run west/southwest from the maze to the same level-38 hut. Inside the correct hut, use the bones on the Chaos Altar until the inventory is gone, then return and repeat. The altar gives the same 350% XP as a gilded altar with both burners lit, and every offered bone has a 50% chance not to be consumed , so a single bone can be offered multiple times. The hut itself is a known PK hotspot, which is why you should take only one inventory of bones per trip. Stop the moment you reach 43 Prayer. Any unused bones stay banked for later. Why this hybrid is recommended: green dragons save time while the Wilderness is quiet; Isle of Souls removes the PK risk when it is not. The Chaos Altar still supplies the enormous Prayer-efficiency gain, but you only risk one small bone inventory at a time instead of your entire gathering grind.

preparation.title: Recover the bars, holy mould and everyday consumables
preparation.text: For five missing iron bars, mine or buy iron ore and smelt at 15 Smithing until five successful bars are banked; normal smelting can fail, so five ore is not a guarantee. Buy a hammer, empty pots and buckets from a general store; ordinary chicken bones work for the four ecto-token worships. Buy the holy mould from Dommik and one ball of wool from Aemad in East Ardougne, or shear sheep north of Lumbridge and spin the wool at the castle's first-floor wheel. These materials are additional to earlier consumed silver and wool. If the ghostspeak amulet is lost, ask Father Urhney in Lumbridge Swamp for another. If the mithril axe was missed, buy exactly that tier at the Woodcutting Guild now that 60 Woodcutting is covered.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: Now that you have 18 Slayer and 30 Ranged , complete Animal Magnetism for its ammunition-saving reward. The other requirements are already covered: The Restless Ghost and Priest in Peril are complete, and the route is far above 19 Crafting / 35 Woodcutting. First complete Ernest the Chicken in Draynor Manor. The quest does not require outside supplies; collect the pressure gauge, rubber tube and oil can inside/around the manor, solve the basement lever puzzle, and return to Professor Oddenstein. Quest Helper is fine for the lever puzzle. Then prepare Animal Magnetism. Bring or obtain: 1 mithril axe — the one bought at the Woodcutting Guild in 1.3 / when you reached 60 Woodcutting. No other axe substitutes for this quest step. 5 unnoted iron bars , hammer and your ghostspeak amulet . 20 ecto-tokens. If you do not already have them, take 4 bones, 4 empty pots and 4 buckets to the Ectofuntus north of Port Phasmatys. Grind the four bones upstairs into bonemeal, fill the four buckets from the slime pool downstairs, worship four times, then talk to a ghost disciple while wearing the ghostspeak amulet. Each worship is worth 5 tokens. 1 hard leather. If missing, tan a cowhide into hard leather at Ellis in Al Kharid. 1 holy symbol. If missing, use the silver bar set aside for a holy symbol in 1.1: make an unblessed symbol with a holy mould, string it with wool, then have Brother Jered upstairs in the Edgeville Monastery bless it. Your 43 Prayer already clears the monastery's 31 Prayer entry requirement. If the bar was spent, refill it at the East Ardougne Silver Merchant first; do not borrow Desert Treasure's bar. Polished buttons. Check the bank first; if missing, pickpocket H.A.M. members in the hideout east of Draynor until you get buttons, then polish them by clicking them. Complete Animal Magnetism from start to finish. At under 50 Ranged, Ava rewards Ava’s attractor . Wear it for the rest of the Ranged grind: it automatically recovers 60% of fired ammunition , another 20% drops to the floor, and 20% breaks. Do not wear a metal torso that interferes with the device. Reserve at least 75 steel arrows. At 50 Ranged, Ava can upgrade the attractor to Ava’s accumulator using 75 steel arrows; the accumulator automatically recovers 72% of fired ammunition. Open the OSRS Wiki Animal Magnetism guide if you want the dialogue/puzzle walkthrough while following this route's preparation list. Before leaving the bank: check the quest-specific quantities and sources in the preparation note.

route_steps.review: Existing resource/level handoff checked against the adjacent quest consumers; do not interpret expected loot as live bank ownership.
route_steps.visible_checkpoint: If you enjoy nearly second-screen combat, stay at Gemstone Crab after 45 Ranged and train melee to 65 Attack, 65 Strength and 65 Defence . Equip the rune sword purchased in 1.3, your amulet of strength , and the best melee armour already in the bank. Attack the crab, leave auto-retaliate on, and move through the nearby cave when the crab relocates roughly every ten minutes. Train the three melee stats in whatever order you prefer. Why 65/65/65? 65 Attack + 65 Strength is exactly the 130 combined needed to enter the Warriors' Guild. 65 Defence already passes the 60 Defence needed to equip a dragon defender and meets the unboosted 65 Defence requirement for King's Ransom. 70 Defence for Piety still comes later. Skip this detour if you would rather continue questing. Chapter 1 works with roughly 46 Attack / 50 Strength / 34 Defence. Chapter 2 includes the extra training for Warriors' Guild access, a dragon defender and King's Ransom when you need it.

preparation.title: Balloon materials and the willow-branch timer
preparation.text: Bring 3 papyrus, 1 ball of wool, 1 full sack of potatoes (10), 8 additional empty sacks, 1 unlit candle, yellow dye, red dye, 10 silk, an empty bowl, 10 normal logs, tinderbox and 12 willow branches . Buy papyrus and wool from Aemad in East Ardougne, sacks from Sarah's farm shop, and an unlit candle from Catherby's candle shop. Pick ten potatoes in the Lumbridge field and fill one sack; the other eight must stay empty. Steal silk from the Ardougne stall or buy it from the Al Kharid silk trader. For dyes, give Aggie in Draynor 3 redberries + 5 coins for red and 2 onions + 5 coins for yellow; Wydin sells redberries and onions grow north of Rimmington. A bowl is available at a general store. Cut the ten ordinary logs; willow logs do not replace the ordinary fuel in this opening flight. Branches are not logs. Auguste supplies a willow seed: use a filled plant pot/trowel/watering can to make its sapling, plant it in a tree patch at 30 Farming and pay the gardener a basket of five apples for protection if desired. Buy the basket from Sarah and apples from a food shop. Once the willow is grown, use secateurs to cut branches, returning for regrowth until you hold twelve; keep the tree standing while doing this. A regular wild willow cannot supply the branches. Other balloon destinations require separate logs later; this quest does not consume the Grand Tree's three-magic-log unlock.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: Complete Enlightened Journey for balloon transport and its 2,000 Crafting XP . The earlier quests have already given you 30 Farming , so there is no extra Farming grind. Go directly to The Hand in the Sand next; A Soul’s Bane follows that quest. Before leaving the bank: check the quest-specific quantities and sources in the preparation note.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: Check your Crafting level first: this quest needs unboosted 49 Crafting and 17 Thieving to start, with no prerequisite quest or mandatory fight. Thieving is already covered. If below 49, blow more of the planned 1,590-orb batch until you reach 49; you already trained the 46 Crafting needed to make orbs in 1.3. You may use banked gems or separately sourced glass for a shortfall, but do not consume quest glass. At 49, blow one lantern lens from the glass reserved for this quest. Bank check before Bert in Yanille: bring about 150 coins , one empty vial (a second makes Zavistic's Port Sarim teleport convenient), one white berry , one lantern lens , five earth runes , and one empty bucket or a bucket of sand. If missing, buy a vial from a Herblore shop, a bucket from a general store and the earth runes from Betty in Port Sarim for 20 coins. Bring one beer and redberries if already banked; otherwise buy the beer at Yanille's Dragon Inn and redberries at Port Sarim's food store during the quest. The quest supplies its own sand from Sandy in Brimhaven; fill the bucket at Yanille's sandpit for the separate final bucket-of-sand step. White-berry fallback now, before Farming Contracts: check the bank first. If none are banked, bring food and kill level-37 chaos druid warriors in the Yanille Agility Dungeon until one drops; the first balancing ledge needs 40 Agility, already covered. The berry is a random drop (listed at 5/128 per kill), so keep going until you have one. This source works without 59 Farming or a Wilderness trip. Do not use the dungeon chaos altar: it drops you into poison spiders. A berry already grown/banked is fine. Start with Bert by the Yanille sandpit , then ring the bell outside the Wizards' Guild to call Zavistic Rarve. You do not need the normal guild-entry Magic level for this quest. Follow Bert's/Sandy's rota and Betty's truth-serum sequence, visit Entrana briefly, and finish the quest for 9,000 Crafting XP , 1,000 Thieving XP and Bert's daily sand option. The current quick guide covers dialogue if needed.

preparation.title: A Soul's Bane needs a rope and a separate combat inventory
preparation.text: Take one rope from Ned in Draynor, food, a teleport and combat gear before entering the rift. The anger weapons, fear/confusion rooms and other special objects are supplied inside the quest. Bring normal combat supplies for the final fight; you do not need to buy or craft the anger weapons beforehand.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: Complete A Soul’s Bane , then finish blowing your unpowered orbs. You will check whether you need more Crafting training at the end of this section. From the 1,600 molten glass made in 1.3, you should now have: 1,590 unpowered orbs 6 molten glass reserved for Desert Treasure 1 molten glass already blown into the lantern lens for The Hand in the Sand 1 molten glass used for the birdhouse crafting table 2 in 1.3, plus up to 2 spare molten glass ; one may have become Pirate Pete's fishbowl, leaving one for Chapter 2 If you split the bankstanding grind across the chapter, finish every remaining unpowered orb now . The 1,590 orbs give 83,475 Crafting XP . Starting orb-blowing at exactly level 46 brings you to 151,458 XP from the orbs alone. Your quest rewards, lens and jewellery add more. Wait before training to 58: finish the remaining quests, then check your Crafting level at the end of this section. Before leaving the bank: check the quest-specific quantities and sources in the preparation note.

route_steps.review: Watchtower supplied locally; the earlier 1.1 cloak checklist is linked for readers with saved progress from the old route. No duplicate quest completion, cat unlock or lamp XP.

preparation.title: Watchtower's bones, ropes and unfinished potion
preparation.text: Watchtower: bring 20 coins, 1 gold bar, 1 death rune, pickaxe, 1 dragon bones, 2 ropes, 1 guam potion (unf), lit candle/lantern, pestle and mortar, 1 bat bones and 1 jangerberries . Use the dragon bone specifically retained after 43 Prayer; if spent, kill one more blue dragon using the earlier shield/safespot setup. Smith one gold ore at 40 Smithing (buy ore from Ordan), buy the rune from Aubury/Betty and ropes from Ned, and kill a bat by Keep Le Faye for the bat bones. A clean guam plus a water-filled vial makes the unfinished potion at 3 Herblore; use Taverley chaos druids if none remains. For jangerberries, use a banked Hosidius fruit-stall berry or use one of the two ropes to reach the ogre island west of Yanille and pick its ground spawn. The second rope remains for the later cave entry. The potion's other special ingredients and the skavid map/crystals come from quest steps; follow the mixing order before giving the mixture to the Watchtower wizard. Keep food and a teleport for Gorad and the ogre caves.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: Complete Watchtower as a standalone quest. Plague City, Biohazard and Ardougne Easy were completed on the first Ardougne visit in 1.1. Missing Ardougne cloak 1? If you have not claimed it yet, complete the early quest and Easy Diary checklist now. Skip any quests or diary tasks you have already completed. If only the cloak was lost, Two-pints in the Flying Horse Inn replaces it for free. Use an unspent diary lamp on Herblore here if eligible; if you used the lamp earlier, continue without it. The optional cat loop from 1.1 already pays 200 death runes per extra adult cat. Keep one grown, non-overgrown cat for RFD Evil Dave before trading extras; raise and trade extra cats only when it fits your session. Before leaving the bank: check the quest-specific quantities and sources in the preparation note.

preparation.title: Light, knife and ammunition
preparation.text: Bring a knife as well as the lit light source to cut the web and collect the boots of lightness. Buy the knife from a general store and a candle from Catherby's candle shop, then light it with a tinderbox. Remove heavy equipment at the bridge and use the quest boots so your carried weight is negative; the boots of lightness are enough for this step without a Graceful outfit. The knife/bow workaround still needs the quest's ice arrow equipped and enough thrown ammunition for the fight. For self-made replacement knives, mine/buy iron ore and smelt until the required bars succeed; earlier quest bars are spent.

route_steps.visible_checkpoint: Check the bank before travelling: bring 20 unnoted limpwurt roots , a light source, weight-reducing gear, and darts or throwing knives . Steel arrows do not replace the thrown ammunition in the Fire Warrior workaround. Count existing knives/darts first; if short, prepare about 50 iron knives as a starter. With the 50 Agility and Thieving from 1.2, buy them from Martin Thwait beneath the Toad and Chicken in Burthorpe's Rogues' Den (only ten stocked per world, so allow restocks or other worlds), or at 22 Smithing use a hammer and anvil to turn 10 iron bars into 50 knives . Make or buy a small starting batch; if combat consumes the first stack, return for only another 25–50. The Kourend diary already spent its separate root; check how many roots remain in the bank. If your flower harvests or seed drops ran short, take ordinary combat gear, food and a Hosidius house teleport to the level-28 hobgoblins on the peninsula north-east of the Hosidius Vinery . Kill them for their repeatable but random limpwurt-root drops, bank the missing roots, and stop exactly when you hold 20. This direct-root recovery needs no limpwurt seeds or extra Farming wait. Then complete Temple of Ikov . You do not need to grind Puro-Puro for a yew longbow. In the ice chamber, search the chests until you obtain at least 1 ice arrow . Equip the ice arrow in your ammo slot, then use darts/throwing knives on the Fire Warrior of Lesarkus; the current quest mechanics allow thrown weapons to bypass the normal yew-bow requirement. Wear Ava's attractor and retrieve recoverable knives when safe, but restock if you run low, since some ammunition still breaks. Before leaving the bank: check the quest-specific quantities and sources in the preparation note.
